benchmark_environment.scope_note: Local microbenchmark measurements executed in the host Python environment. Measurements evaluate single-threaded in-memory execution.

measured_microbenchmarks.name: Direct Unprotected Baseline
measured_microbenchmarks.description: Direct synthetic Python lambda invocation without firewall interception
measured_microbenchmarks.context_note: A minimal in-memory Python lambda taking ~0.3 microseconds. Real-world tools with network or disk I/O typically take 5-50 ms.

measured_microbenchmarks.name: Fast-Path PROHIBIT (Demo B)
measured_microbenchmarks.description: Security intercept: tool validation, deterministic policy evaluation to PROHIBIT, session terminal event, audit append (no token, no execution)

measured_microbenchmarks.name: Review Ticket Creation (Demo C initial)
measured_microbenchmarks.description: Policy evaluation resulting in REVIEW, ReviewerView projection, ticket generation, state-head snapshot, audit append

measured_microbenchmarks.name: Review Resolution & Execution (Demo C resolve)
measured_microbenchmarks.description: Ticket retrieval, state freshness check, policy re-evaluation, HMAC capability token minting, ControlledExecutor execution, audit append

measured_microbenchmarks.name: Fast-Path PERMIT (Demo A)
measured_microbenchmarks.description: Full gateway interception: action parsing, registry lookup, policy evaluation, state update, HMAC token issue, ControlledExecutor execution, audit append

analytical_stage_estimates.basis: Architectural breakdown estimating internal distribution of the 0.94 ms Fast-Path PERMIT turn. Stages were not timed via separate hardware counters in bench.py.

external_comparisons.name: Local Sentence Transformers Semantic Monitor (CPU)
external_comparisons.note: Derived from prior project literature and pilot experiments; not measured in the local bench.py microbenchmark.

external_comparisons.name: Local/Cloud LLM Risk Monitor (Ollama / Remote API)
external_comparisons.note: Representative external LLM call latency (network round-trip + token generation); not measured in the local bench.py microbenchmark. Relative speedup claims (e.g. 663x) are external comparisons, not experimentally measured speedups.

resource_and_concurrency_notes.status_note: No CPU utilization, memory consumption, or multi-threaded throughput tests exist in bench.py. All microbenchmarks reflect single-threaded execution.
